def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space:
## Definition

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.
def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, with the geometric meaning fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the future-cone field called $N$ in that definition. A **temporal product chart** is a smooth coordinate map from an open product $I\times\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ onto an open subset of $M$, with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$. We require $x^0$ to have length units and each $x^i$ to have length units in the physical interpretation.

The chart has **lapse-shift data** $(N,\beta,h)$ when $N:I\times\Omega\to(0,\infty)$, $\beta^i:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $h_{ij}:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$, and the matrix $(h_{ij})$ is positive definite at each point, with

$$g=-N^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i dx^0)(dx^j+\beta^j dx^0).$$

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. The normal field is

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. This definition is local to the specified product chart; it asserts no global temporal foliation.
def-rpm-h-almost-regular-legendre:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantitie.physical_scope: Classical spinless test-particle quantities on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. Mass and c are primitive parameters of this model; no particle action, force law, backreaction, empirical result, or universal identification with another framework is included.

def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantitie:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.
def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.
thm-rpm-h-canonical-poisson-and-flow:
## Statement

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Classical spinless structureless point test body with fixed primitive mass m>0 on a prescribed background; excludes self-field, radiation reaction, finite size, spin and quantum effects.

post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

For a $C^2$ future-directed timelike worldline $x:I\to M$ on a prescribed smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,T)$ of signature $(-+++)$, with $m>0$ a fixed primitive mass in kg and $c>0$ in m/s, adopt the stationary-action model

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int_I\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here λ is an increasing regular parameter, endpoint events are fixed, and admissible variations remain future timelike. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_m=-mc^2\int d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. It is neither a theorem about all matter nor an empirical report, and supplies no backreaction or completeness claim. The flat ideal-clock specialization agrees with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; adopting this action on a curved background remains a separate premise.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action.physical_scope: Separate classical massless test-particle formulation with nonzero future-null momentum; no proper-time parameter, no mU identification and no empirical realization claim.

post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action:
## Postulate

On a prescribed background $(M,g,T)$, adopt a distinct massless classical particle model with fields $x:I\to M$, $p(\lambda)\in T^*_{x(\lambda)}M$, and a positive smooth multiplier $e(\lambda)>0$:

$$S_0[x,p,e]=\int_I\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Variations of $p,e$ are independent; the physical branch is $p\ne0$, $p^\sharp$ future null. With all spacetime coordinates measured in metres and dimensionless λ, $p_a$ has units kg m/s, $C_0$ has units kg²m²/s² and $e$ has units s/kg, making the action J s. Other parameter units scale $e$ accordingly. This is a separate adopted model: null curves have no proper-time parameter, the model does not arise by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, and its positive momentum scale is additional initial data. On the nonzero branch, the vertical differential is $d_pC_0=p^\sharp\ne0$: nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p\ne0$ give $p^\sharp\ne0$. Hence the shell is a regular primary constraint in the sense of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. This postulate is not an empirical observation or a deduction from the massive model.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.
thm-rpm-h-constraint-consistency:
## Statement

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $(P,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold. Let $\chi_a:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and suppose the covectors $d_z\chi_a(\lambda,z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in N_\lambda:=\{z:\chi_1(\lambda,z)=\cdots=\chi_r(\lambda,z)=0\}$; this is the regular constraint condition of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]] on each slice. Let $H_c:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth ambient extension of a specified descended Hamiltonian. Work in a Darboux chart with coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$ and local potential $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$, so $d\theta=-\omega$ under the convention $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$; paths stay in this chart.
For any compact interval $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, paths $z:[a,b]\to P$ that stay in the chart and smooth multipliers $u^a:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ have action

$$I[z,u]=\int_a^b\left[\theta(\dot z)-H_c(\lambda,z)-u^a(\lambda)\chi_a(\lambda,z)\right]d\lambda.$$

Fixed-endpoint variations of $z$ and unrestricted variations of $u$ imply $z(\lambda)\in N_\lambda$ and $\dot z=X_{H_c(\lambda,\cdot)}+u^a(\lambda)X_{\chi_a(\lambda,\cdot)}$. A trajectory remains in the moving level set only when

$$\partial_\lambda\chi_a+\{\chi_a,H_c(\lambda,\cdot)\}+u^b(\lambda)\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0\quad\text{on }N_\lambda.$$

For constraints independent of $\lambda$, the first term is zero.
thm-rpm-h-first-class-local-reduction:
## Statement

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.
thm-rpm-h-homogeneous-legendre-degenerac:
## Statement

Let $L(q,v)$ be $C^2$ on a conic open subset of a tangent bundle, and suppose $L(q,av)=aL(q,v)$ for every $a>0$ in its domain. At each nonzero $v$,

$$v^iL_{v^i}=L,\qquad L_{v^iv^j}v^i=0,\qquad E_L:=v^iL_{v^i}-L=0.$$

Consequently the velocity Hessian is singular and the fibre derivative cannot be a local diffeomorphism there; a regular Legendre equivalence theorem cannot be applied. These conclusions do not imply that the motion is static or that the Lagrangian has a specified constraint surface.
thm-rpm-h-local-legendre-and-energy-desc:
## Statement

Let $L(t,q,v)$ be smooth on an open velocity domain and let $\mathbb FL(t,q,v)=(t,q,L_v)$ be almost regular in the sense that it is a surjective submersion onto a specified embedded image $N$ and every fibre is connected. Define $E_L=v^iL_{v^i}-L$. Then there is a unique smooth function $h:N\to\mathbb R$ with $E_L=h\circ\mathbb FL$. The assertion is local in the stated domains; no global inverse velocity map is asserted.
thm-rpm-h-second-class-dirac-bracket:
## Statement

Let $(P,\omega)$ be symplectic and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_{2k}$ be smooth on an open set $U$, with $C_{ab}=\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}$ invertible at every point of $U$. Write $C^{ab}$ for its inverse and $N=\{\chi=0\}\cap U$. Then $N$ is an embedded symplectic submanifold, and the bracket

$$\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_a\}C^{ab}\{\chi_b,G\}$$

is the Poisson bracket of the restricted symplectic form on $N$. It is independent of ambient extensions of $F,G$, and every $\chi_a$ is a Casimir. This is local and assumes invertibility on $U$; it does not cover singular points.
thm-rpm-h-flat-shell-global-reduction:
## Statement

In affine Minkowski space with inertial coordinates $x^0,x^i$ measured in metres and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, let $m\ge0$ and let

$$\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p): -p_0=P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2},\ p_0<0\},$$

where $\mathbf p\ne0$ when $m=0$, and write $P^i=p_i$ for the spatial raised momentum components. The characteristic flow of the restricted canonical form is $(x,p)\mapsto(x+\alpha P,p)$, and its orbit space is globally diffeomorphic to $B_m=\mathbb R^3_a\times\mathbb R^3_p$ for $m>0$, or $\mathbb R^3_a\times(\mathbb R^3_p\setminus\{0\})$ for $m=0$, by

$$a^i=x^i-\frac{P^i}{P^0}x^0,\qquad p_i=p_i.$$

The reduced symplectic form is $da^i\wedge dp_i$. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable and each full characteristic line meets each slice $x^0=ct$ exactly once. This is an explicit free flat quotient, not a conclusion about arbitrary first-class systems.
thm-rpm-h-homogeneous-massive-shell:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $m,c>0$, and $L(x,V)=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ on the future timelike tangent cone. Its fibre derivative is

$$p_a=mc\frac{g_{ab}V^b}{s},\qquad s=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}>0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.
thm-rpm-h-regular-local-gauge-slice:
## Statement

Let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ be regular first-class constraints on $N$ as in [[thm-rpm-h-first-class-local-reduction]]. Let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_r$ be smooth gauge functions such that $A_{ab}=\{\chi_a,\phi_b\}$ is invertible on their common zero set near a point. Then the combined constraint matrix for $(\chi,\phi)$ is invertible there, so the combined surface is second class and carries the Dirac symplectic form. After shrinking the neighborhood, each nearby characteristic leaf intersects the gauge surface in exactly one point within that coordinate neighborhood. This is a local slice assertion only. When $r=0$ the characteristic leaves are points and the empty gauge condition is immediate; the proof below treats $r\ge1$.
thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesi:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-+++)$. Work in a spacetime chart on a compact parameter interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$; take $x,p,e$ smooth on a neighbourhood of that interval, $e>0$, $m\ge0$, and $c>0$. Select stationary triples on the future shell branch after taking the independent variations: when $m>0$, $p^\sharp$ is future timelike; when $m=0$, require $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ future null. Set $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ and define the first-order functional

$$I_m[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left(p_ax'^a-eC_m(x,p)\right)d\lambda.$$

Take independent smooth variations of $p,e$ and fixed-endpoint variations of $x$. Stationarity on the chart segment is equivalent to

$$x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b,\quad p'_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c,\quad C_m=0.$$

On the massive future branch $m>0$, these equations are equivalent to stationary paths of the mathematical square-root functional $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(x\prime,x\prime)}\,d\lambda$ on future-timelike curves with fixed endpoints; the fibre-derivative covector is $p=mc\,x'^\flat/\sqrt{-g(x',x')}$, and proper-time gauge has $e=1/m$. For the separate nonzero future-null branch $m=0$, the equations describe a null geodesic with an arbitrary positive parameter multiplier; no proper-time parameter exists. In both cases the unparameterized path is a geodesic, and no existence or completeness claim is made.
thm-rpm-h-inertial-time-reduced-hamilton:
## Statement

In affine Minkowski space with $x^0=ct$, let $m\ge0$, $p_i$ be spatial momentum components and $p_i\ne0$ for $m=0$. On the future shell, $p_0=-E/c$, where

$$E(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}.$$

On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ of inertial time, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order shell action to

$$I_J=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(p_i\dot q^i-E(\mathbf p)\right)dt,\qquad q^i=x^i.$$

The gauge pair $C_m=0$, $\psi=x^0-ct=0$ is second class because $\{C_m,\psi\}=-P^0\ne0$ on the future shell; its Dirac reduction gives the canonical spatial bracket. The reduced Hamilton equations are $\dot q^i=c^2p_i/E$, $\dot p_i=0$, agreeing with the unreduced characteristic trajectories. On this full flat future shell every characteristic line meets each inertial-time slice once; this global assertion does not extend by this proof to a curved temporal chart.

pthm-rpm-h-action-mechanical-momentum.physical_scope: Identity in the adopted massive point-particle model; the SR supplier is used only for the explicitly flat consistency check.

pthm-rpm-h-action-mechanical-momentum:
## Statement

For the massive square-root Lagrangian $L=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ on a prescribed smooth Lorentzian background, its fibre derivative is $p=mc\,V^\flat/\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$. If τ is proper time along the timelike curve, $U=dx/d\tau=cV/\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$, so the raised momentum is $p^\sharp=mU$. In flat spacetime this agrees with the adopted special-relativistic mechanical momentum convention. This is a model identity, not a measurement.

pthm-rpm-h-massive-and-null-time-motion.physical_scope: Conditional flat-spacetime kinematic prediction of the two adopted free models; no empirical speed measurement is claimed.

pthm-rpm-h-massive-and-null-time-motion:
## Statement

In the flat inertial-time model of [[thm-rpm-h-inertial-time-reduced-hamiltonian]], the coordinate velocity is $\dot{\mathbf q}=c^2\mathbf p/E$. For $m>0$, its Euclidean magnitude is strictly less than $c$; for the separate massless model $m=0$ with $\mathbf p\ne0$, its magnitude is exactly $c$. Spatial momentum is constant in both cases. These are deductions from the adopted free actions, not experimental measurements.
thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction:
## Statement

Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. On the future shell $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)=0$, define

$$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

For $m=0$, require $p_i\ne0$. On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ whose path stays in the chart, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order action to $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(p_i\dot q^i-H)dt$, and its variational equations on the interior of $J$ are exactly $\dot q^i=H_{p_i}$, $\dot p_i=-H_{q^i}$. The construction is local to this chart and intervals transverse to its time slices; no global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

pthm-rpm-h-coordinate-versus-observer-en.physical_scope: Conditional energy identities in a supplied temporal chart; SR is used only as a flat consistency specialization, not as a curved premise.

pthm-rpm-h-coordinate-versus-observer-en:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]], the future unit normal $n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i)$ measures positive particle energy

$$E_n=-c\,p(n)=c\kappa,$$

while the chart's reduced Hamiltonian is $H=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i)$. The normal-frame spatial velocity is $w^i=(\dot q^i/c+\beta^i)/N=h^{ij}p_j/\kappa$, with $h_{ij}w^iw^j<1$ for $m>0$ and $=1$ for a nonzero massless state. Write $|\beta|_h:=\sqrt{h_{ij}\beta^i\beta^j}$ and $|p|_{h^{-1}}:=\sqrt{h^{ij}p_ip_j}$. If $\beta^2:=h_{ij}\beta^i\beta^j<N^2$, then $H>0$. If $\beta^2>N^2$, $H$ can be negative even though $E_n>0$. Along a Hamiltonian solution, $dH/dt=\partial_tH$; only explicit time independence implies its conservation.

ex-rpm-h-shifted-chart-negative-energy.physical_scope: Conditional flat-metric coordinate example using the adopted normal-observer energy convention and the stated future massive shell; no measurement, empirical inference or curved-background claim.
